sources.name: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet
sources.used_for: gravity, temperature, distance in million km, Moon's distance from Earth

sources.name: NASA Mission Viz: orbital parameters table
sources.used_for: sma_au (distance from the Sun in AU) and period_days (length of a year), used for food and real trip times

rules.fuel: gravity (m/s^2) x 10 to land, and the same again to take off  -> stronger gravity = more fuel
rules.food: sma_au (distance from Sun in AU, Mission Viz) x 10 each way  -> farther = more food
rules.heater_cooler: a heater if it ever gets colder than -50 C, a cooler if it ever gets hotter than 50 C (10 points each)
rules.budget: how many points of fuel, food and gear the rocket can carry on this mission
rules.temp_min_max: coldest and hottest surface temperature in C, from NASA's Moon, Mars and Europa pages
rules.trip_days: Hohmann transfer from Earth: 0.5 x ((1 + sma_au) / 2)^1.5 x Earth's period_days. The Moon isn't in the Mission Viz table, so its trip uses the 3 days Apollo crews took. Europa orbits Jupiter, so it uses Jupiter's row.
rules.minutes: time on the surface to collect information (team idea: 3, 2, 1)
rules.from_earth: closest distance from Earth in million km (Moon: 0.384 from the fact sheet; planets: their distance from the Sun minus Earth's 149.6)

real_mission.name: Apollo 11
real_mission.note: Apollo 11 launched on July 16, 1969 and reached the Moon 3 days later, just like your trip.

real_mission.name: Perseverance rover
real_mission.note: Perseverance launched on July 30, 2020 and landed on February 18, 2021: 203 days. Real missions launch when Earth and Mars line up and take a slightly faster path than a perfect Hohmann transfer.

real_mission.name: Europa Clipper
real_mission.note: Europa Clipper launched in October 2024 and reaches Jupiter in 2030, about 5.5 years. It flies past Mars and Earth first for gravity assists: a longer path that saves fuel, because no rocket could carry enough for the direct trip.

levels.note: Europa is a moon of Jupiter. It isn't in the Mission Viz table, so its distance, year and trip time use Jupiter's row. Gravity and temperature: check on NASA's Europa page.
